NEW YORK - Comcast Corp ( CMCSA.O ) lost more video subscribers than expected in the fourth quarter due to stiffer competition from phone companies, and said it would not complete its share buyback program this year, pushing its shares down 5 percent.

text: Best Buy CEO sets goals; Wall Street begs for more details. - Best Buy Co Inc ( BBY.N ) hopes to triple its operating margins over time, the company said on Tuesday, though investors and analysts were left wanting for details on how - and how soon - the new chief executive would turn around the world's largest consumer electronics chain.

text: U.S. judge in Libor cases puts new lawsuits on hold. NEW YORK - A federal judge on Wednesday suspended several new lawsuits that allege banks rigged key interest rates, saying she first needed to sort through the issues in an earlier round of related lawsuits.

title: China factory sector shrinks most in 32 months
text: China factory sector shrinks most in 32 months. BEIJING - China's factory sector shrank the most in 32 months in November on signs of domestic economic weakness, a preliminary PMI survey showed, reviving worries that China may be slipping toward a hard landing and fuelling fears of a global recession.

text: S&P 500 extends rally to day five with slim gain. NEW YORK - The Standard & Poor's 500 extended its rally to a fifth day on Thursday, again eking out a tiny gain as lingering expectations for economic stimulus from central banks lent support to a market lacking new catalysts.

text: Exclusive: UBS, State Street discussed asset management merger. NEW YORK - UBS was in talks with State Street Corp about a possible combination of their asset management businesses, but those talks fell through in June, according to two people familiar with the situation.

text: China sees factory growth slowing slightly in 2012. text: Two bids submitted for Clear Channel: sources. NEW YORK - Clear Channel Communications Inc. ( CCU.N ), the No. 1 U.S. radio company, was evaluating takeover proposals on Tuesday after two bids were submitted by separate private equity consortiums, sources familiar with the situation said.

title: EU/IMF start Portugal bailout review, focus on slippage
text: EU/IMF start Portugal bailout review, focus on slippage. LISBON - EU and IMF officials launched their first review of Portugal's international bailout on Monday, with the focus on how the government plans to correct a budget slippage and meet its promised fiscal targets this year.

text: Thanksgiving kicks off fight for holiday sales. - The holiday shopping season is in full swing on Thursday, with retailers hoping consumers will spend big despite worries about the fragile economy and their own precarious finances.

title: EU's Kroes: euro zone can live without Greece: media
text: EU's Kroes: euro zone can live without Greece: media. AMSTERDAM - The euro zone can survive even if Greece is forced out, European Commissioner Neelie Kroes said in an newspaper interview on Tuesday as Greek leaders struggled to secure a 130-billion-euro ($170 billion) bailout and avert further crisis.

title: Portugal union leader wants debt renegotiation
text: Portugal union leader wants debt renegotiation. LISBON - Portugal must renegotiate its debts rather than impose harsh austerity measures to overcome its economic crisis, the head of the country's largest trade union said on Wednesday, threatening to step up strikes if the government pushed on with cuts.

text: Instant view: Apple takes wraps off sleek new iPhone. NEW YORK - Apple Inc, firing the latest salvo in the smartphone wars, rolled out a slim new version of its wildly popular iPhone on Monday.

title: KKR-led group has deal to buy Samson for $7.2 billion
text: KKR-led group has deal to buy Samson for $7.2 billion. - A consortium led by private equity firm KKR & Co ( KKR.N ) clinched a deal to buy oil and gas group Samson Investment Co for $7.2 billion, KKR said on Wednesday.

text: Factory growth slows, casts shadow on economy. WASHINGTON - Manufacturing grew at its slowest pace in two years in July as new orders contracted, casting doubt on expectations the faltering recovery would quickly regain steam.

text: Global search for Tata chairman ends close to home. MUMBAI - The next chairman of India's venerable salt-to-software conglomerate Tata Group will be an insider and a family member by marriage.

text: Labor unrest taking shine off Colombia's oil boom. PUERTO GAITAN, Colombia - Protesting oil workers have yet to buy into Colombia's grand vision for its oil industry, staging strikes that have shut the country's largest oil field and threatening further unrest.

text: Oil rallies to record near $120 on supply worries. NEW YORK - Oil surged to records near $120 a barrel on Tuesday on the weaker dollar, export disruptions from Nigerian rebel attacks and concerns a Scottish refinery strike could hit North Sea production.

text: POSCO consortium eyes $1 billion stake in ArcelorMittal Canada mine: report. SEOUL - A consortium including South Korean steelmaker POSCO ( 005490.KS ) is seeking to acquire a roughly $1 billion stake in a Canadian iron ore mine operator controlled by ArcelorMittal ( ISPA.AS ), South Korean financial publication Money Today reported on Wednesday.

text: State Street battles weak FX revenue, high compensation costs. - Weak foreign exchange revenue persists at State Street Corp ( STT.N ), hurting the custody bank's chances of lowering its high ratio of compensation expenses, top executives said on Tuesday.

title: James Turley to retire as Ernst & Young CEO
text: James Turley to retire as Ernst & Young CEO. - Accounting and consulting firm Ernst & Young said chairman and chief executive James Turley will retire in June 2013.

text: France says ECB independence very important. PARIS - France, like Germany, attaches great importance to the European Central Bank's independence, French Finance Minister Francois Baroin said on Thursday.

text: Baer says Merrill Lynch unit integration on track. ZURICH - Julius Baer ( BAER.VX ) has transferred ownership of businesses in Chile, Uruguay, Monaco and Luxembourg which it bought from Merrill Lynch ( BAC.N ) as it integrates the wealth management businesses it acquired from the U.S. bank.

text: Latin Americans fret as Stanford crisis spreads. CARACAS - Well-off Mexican pensioners joined middle-class Venezuelans in a frantic quest on Wednesday to track down their savings as the fraud scandal enveloping U.S. broker Stanford Group Co spread to Latin America.

text: ANA to put pilots through Dreamliner resumption training: sources. TOKYO - Toyota Motor Corp ( 7203.T ) said it will recall around 2.77 million vehicles worldwide, including certain models of the Prius, due to problems with the steering mechanism and the hybrid system water pump, its second multi-million car recall in two months.

title: Boeing first-quarter deliveries rise 8 percent

title: Children's Place, Disney unit settle store dispute

text: Intrepid Potash IPO raises $960 million. NEW YORK - Intrepid Potash Inc, a producer of crop nutrients, on Monday raised $960 million with an initial public offering of shares that priced above expectations.

title: XTO Energy CEO sees more acquisitions this year
text: XTO Energy CEO sees more acquisitions this year. HOUSTON - The chief executive officer of XTO Energy Inc XTO.N said on Tuesday he expects the company to spend at least $1 billion to $1.5 billion on additional acquisitions in 2008.

title: Other possible Dow Jones bidders surface
text: Other possible Dow Jones bidders surface. NEW YORK - An Internet entrepreneur and a Wall Street group have joined a list of potential rivals to News Corp.'s NWSa.N $5 billion bid for Wall Street Journal publisher Dow Jones & Co. Inc. DJ.N, an adviser to the Dow Jones employee union said on Thursday.

title: Lehman enters Qatar to expand Middle East push
text: Lehman enters Qatar to expand Middle East push. LONDON - U.S. bank Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. LEH.N has been granted a license to operate in Qatar, where it plans to expand its Middle East business after it moved into Dubai last year.

title: INSTANT VIEW 6-BOJ tankan shows optimism declines

title: Sears securitizes its brand names: BusinessWeek
text: Sears securitizes its brand names: BusinessWeek. NEW YORK - Sears Holdings Corp. ( SHLD.O ) has created $1.8 billion worth of securities based on its most famous brand names: Kenmore, Craftsman and Die Hard, BusinessWeek magazine said in its latest issue on Thursday.

title: Greece says will get aid tranche after review in mid-September
text: Greece says will get aid tranche after review in mid-September. ATHENS - Greece expects to get its next tranche of international aid immediately lenders give their final verdict in mid-September on progress made under its bailout program, a deputy finance minister said on Thursday.

title: Dow Jones closes at all-time high
text: Dow Jones closes at all-time high. NEW YORK - U.S. stocks rallied on Tuesday, pushing the Dow to a record closing high, after Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and Target Corp. posted stronger-than-expected profits and inflation data eased interest-rate concerns.

title: New Century files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
text: New Century files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. NEW YORK - New Century Financial Corp. filed for bankruptcy protection on Monday amid a surge in homeowner defaults, the biggest mortgage lender to collapse in the slumping U.S. housing market.

title: Goldman's senior metals trader Evans leaves bank: sources
text: Goldman's senior metals trader Evans leaves bank: sources. NEW YORK - Goldman Sachs' ( GS.N ) senior physical metals trader Scott Evans has left the U.S. investment bank in New York, becoming the second high-profile member of the physical base metals team to depart since mid-March, sources told Reuters.

title: Lowe's posts profit drop, cuts store openings
text: Lowe's posts profit drop, cuts store openings. ATLANTA - Lowe's Cos ( LOW.N ) reported a sharp drop in quarterly profit on Friday as it marked down prices in the recession and it gave profit forecasts that fell short of Wall Street estimates, sending shares down 3 percent.

title: J.C. Penney profit tops view; sees Q1 loss
text: J.C. Penney profit tops view; sees Q1 loss. NEW YORK - Department store operator J.C. Penney Co Inc ( JCP.N ) posted a 51 percent drop in fourth quarter profit on Friday, and said its loss in the current quarter would be deeper than Wall Street estimates as shoppers hold off on spending.

title: Lowe's posts sharp drop in profit
text: Lowe's posts sharp drop in profit. ATLANTA - Lowe's Cos ( LOW.N ) reported a sharp drop in quarterly profit on Friday as it marked down prices to lure consumers in the recession and it gave profit forecasts that fell short of Wall Street estimates.

title: Darden Restaurants sales mixed in March
text: Darden Restaurants sales mixed in March. NEW YORK - Darden Restaurants Inc. ( DRI.N ) said on Thursday that same-store sales at its Olive Garden restaurants rose 3 percent to 4 percent in March, while same-store sales at Red Lobster fell about 3 percent.

title: U.S. investor Brandes cut Volkswagen stake -paper
text: U.S. investor Brandes cut Volkswagen stake -paper. FRANKFURT - U.S. financial investor Brandes Investment Partners has apparently cut its stake in German car maker Volkswagen ( VOWG.DE ) to less than 5 percent recently, a German newspaper said on Monday.

title: Rising rates bring first clouds to merger boom
text: Rising rates bring first clouds to merger boom. LONDON - The leveraged buyouts that have fuelled record merger activity face a new test as interest rates rise and stock markets wobble, early signs that the debt behind the deals could become more costly and difficult to raise.

title: Court upholds Netflix "throttling" settlement
text: Court upholds Netflix "throttling" settlement. LOS ANGELES - A California appeals court has upheld a 2006 settlement of a consumer lawsuit against online movie rental company Netflix Inc over the objections of four Netflix subscribers who challenged the terms.

title: BOJ's Kuroda: monetary onslaught won't cause asset bubbles
text: BOJ's Kuroda: monetary onslaught won't cause asset bubbles. TOKYO - Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda played down concerns his unprecedented burst of monetary stimulus would create asset-price bubbles even as it delivered an immediate pay-off in global markets, with government bond yields at a record low, the yen hitting a 3-1/2 year trough and stocks surging to multi-year highs.

title: Fisker Automotive fires most rank-and-file employees
text: Fisker Automotive fires most rank-and-file employees. DETROIT - Fisker Automotive, the struggling, government-backed hybrid sports car maker, terminated most of its rank-and-file employees on Friday, in a last-ditch effort to conserve cash and stave off a potential bankruptcy filing, sources said.

title: U.S. Postal Service loses $5.2 billion, warns of low cash
text: U.S. Postal Service loses $5.2 billion, warns of low cash. WASHINGTON - The U.S. Postal Service's net loss widened to $5.2 billion during the April through June period, and the cash-strapped agency warned on Thursday that without help from the U.S. Congress it will face low cash and be unable to borrow money this fall.

text: Blackstone and LLOG Exploration to invest $1.2 billion. - Private equity firm Blackstone Group LP ( BX.N ) and LLOG Exploration Company LLC will jointly invest $1.2 billion to strengthen the offshore oil producer's operations in Mexico, the two firms said on Tuesday.

text: FACTBOX: Global financial job cuts - many more to come. - Swiss bank Credit Suisse ( CSGN.VX ) said on Tuesday it would axe about 500 more jobs across its investment banking and shared services divisions.

text: Swedish government: Door not closed to Saab loan guarantees. STOCKHOLM - The Swedish government has not closed the door to providing loan guarantees to Saab following a restructuring of General Motors' loss-making Swedish carmaker, a senior official told Reuters on Friday.

title: U.S. housing starts, permits plumb record lows
text: U.S. housing starts, permits plumb record lows. WASHINGTON - U.S. housing starts and building permits dropped to record lows in January, data showed on Wednesday, as builders shelved construction plans to try to clear a glut of unsold houses caused by a slump in demand.

text: Ford CEO Mulally gets $39.1 million compensation. DETROIT - Ford Motor Co. ( F.N ) on Thursday said it awarded new Chief Executive Alan Mulally compensation of $39.1 million for four months of work in 2006, a year when the second-largest U.S. automaker posted a $12.7 billion loss.

text: XTO Energy to buy Hunt Petroleum for $4.2 billion. NEW YORK - XTO Energy Inc XTO.N said on Tuesday that it would buy crude oil and natural gas producer Hunt Petroleum Corp for $4.19 billion in cash and stock in its second major purchase in two weeks.

text: Comcast's NBCUniversal unit lays off 500 employees: source. text: Merrill CEO sees Wall St firms less lucrative. NEW YORK - Wall Street banks will emerge from the credit crunch a little smaller and a little less profitable, Merrill Lynch Chief Executive John Thain told Reuters on Tuesday.

text: Abercrombie shares soar as inventory issues wane. - Teen clothing retailer Abercrombie & Fitch Co ( ANF.N ) stunned investors on Wednesday with unexpectedly improved third-quarter results and a full-year outlook that exceeded Wall Street forecasts, sending shares up as much as 30 percent.

RIN.AX, paving the way for Cemex to make its next move in the drawn-out takeover battle.

title: Cyprus currency decree eases restrictions on bank transfers

title: Thousands of tech faithful snap up first iPhones
text: Thousands of tech faithful snap up first iPhones. SAN FRANCISCO/NEW YORK - Thousands of U.S. gadget fans flocked to stores on Friday to be the first buyers of Apple's iPhone, a music-playing and Web-browsing device expected to shake up the mobile industry.

title: JPMorgan files formal first-quarter restatement
text: JPMorgan files formal first-quarter restatement. - JPMorgan Chase & Co ( JPM.N ) filed a formal restatement of its first-quarter results on Thursday to reflect its conclusion that the values of derivatives positions on a London trading desk were originally overstated.

title: Obama speech on home mortgage crisis
text: Obama speech on home mortgage crisis. "Today, as a result of declining home values, millions of families are "underwater," which means they owe more on their mortgages than their homes are worth. These families are unable to sell their homes, and unable to refinance them. So in the event of a job loss or another emergency, their options are limited.

title: INSTANT VIEW: Automakers', UAW restructuring plans
text: INSTANT VIEW: Automakers', UAW restructuring plans. NEW YORK - The three major U.S. automakers and the United Auto Workers union announced a series of sweeping restructuring plans on Tuesday as the industry looks to plot a roadmap to survival.

title: S&P: GM, Chrysler could face "selective default"
text: S&P: GM, Chrysler could face "selective default". NEW YORK - A distressed debt-for-equity swap for automakers General Motors Corp and Chrysler would lead to a "selective default" for the companies, but their ratings could climb to the "CCC" range upon completion of the bond exchange, Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday.

title: Irish consumer sentiment hits two-year high in July
text: Irish consumer sentiment hits two-year high in July. DUBLIN - Irish consumer sentiment hit a two-year high in July on more positive economic news in Ireland and as fears of a major escalation of the euro zone debt crisis receded.

title: GE's Immelt pay cut, declines bonus
text: GE's Immelt pay cut, declines bonus. BOSTON - General Electric Co paid Chief Executive Jeff Immelt 28 percent less last year as the U.S. conglomerate's top executive asked for no bonus in light of the drop in GE's profits and stock price.

title: Global watchdog official says banking reforms must proceed
text: Global watchdog official says banking reforms must proceed. TORONTO - The underperforming global economy should not be allowed to delay financial system reforms, a senior official at the Financial Stability Board (FSB), a global watchdog set up by the Group of 20 nations, said on Tuesday, adding that the FSB will propose new rules on so-called shadow banking by year-end.

title: Housing plan bolsters Fannie, Freddie: Geithner
text: Housing plan bolsters Fannie, Freddie: Geithner. MESA, Arizona - The Obama administration's plan to reduce mortgage payments for struggling homeowners is expected to help mortgage finance companies Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, U.S. Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner said on Wednesday.

title: Lehman stock slumps again on loss warning
text: Lehman stock slumps again on loss warning. BOSTON - Shares of Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc LEH.N fell more than 7 percent to their lowest level in more than five years on Tuesday, a day after the investment bank raised dilutive capital and warned of a $2.8 billion quarterly loss.

title: McCain wants low corporate taxes, regulated CEO pay
text: McCain wants low corporate taxes, regulated CEO pay. WASHINGTON - Republican White House candidate John McCain will promise on Tuesday to lower corporate tax rates if he wins the U.S. presidency and ease the tax burden on middle-class workers to help revive the faltering economy.

title: Countrywide says housing slump has a year to go
text: Countrywide says housing slump has a year to go. NEW YORK - The slowdown of the U.S. housing market will last through 2007 as inventories are pared enough to prompt a change in consumer psychology, the chief executive officer of the nation's biggest mortgage lender said on Tuesday.

title: Walgreen to shun new CVS Caremark drug plans
text: Walgreen to shun new CVS Caremark drug plans. NEW YORK - Walgreen Co ( WAG.N ) said it will not be a provider for any new or renewed drug plans handled by CVS Caremark Corp's ( CVS.N ) pharmacy benefits manager, which it said favors CVS pharmacies.

title: Exclusive: Astenbeck, Clive funds slide as fiscal cliff hits oil
text: Exclusive: Astenbeck, Clive funds slide as fiscal cliff hits oil. - Astenbeck Capital's Andrew Hall and Clive Capital's Chris Levett -- two of the biggest fund managers in oil -- are in for a second year of losses unless they can steer a turn around the next six weeks in a market bogged down by U.S. fiscal worries.

title: Swiss risk deflation if euro crisis worsens: Jordan
text: Swiss risk deflation if euro crisis worsens: Jordan. GENEVA/ZURICH - The Swiss National Bank fears that an escalation of the euro zone's debt crisis could prompt deflation, Thomas Jordan said in his first speech since becoming interim chairman of the central bank, stressing his determination to keep a lid on the franc.

title: U.S. home prices fall, but rate slows: report
text: U.S. home prices fall, but rate slows: report. NEW YORK - The value of U.S. homes fell by 12.1 percent in the second quarter from a year earlier, but the rate of decline shrank for the first time since prices began to fall in 2007, real estate website Zillow.com said on Tuesday.

title: Goldman chief outlines risky asset reduction under new rules
text: Goldman chief outlines risky asset reduction under new rules. - Goldman Sachs Group Inc ( GS.N ) would have $728 billion in risk-weighted assets under yet-to-be-implemented Basel III capital rules, 67 percent more than the investment bank has under current regulations, Chief Executive Lloyd Blankfein said on Tuesday.

title: Wyeth profit hurt by generic, but beats forecast
text: Wyeth profit hurt by generic, but beats forecast. NEW YORK - Wyeth posted slightly lower first-quarter earnings on Tuesday, hurt by the recent launch of generic forms of its Protonix ulcer drug, but surprisingly strong sales of other medicines enabled the company to beat Wall Street profit forecasts.

title: Former Swiss president quits Stanford board
text: Former Swiss president quits Stanford board. ZURICH - Former Swiss President Adolf Ogi said he is stepping down from the advisory board of Stanford Financial Group after Texas billionaire Allen Stanford and three of his companies were charged with fraud.

title: Deere says to acquire tractor manufacturer in China
text: Deere says to acquire tractor manufacturer in China. - Deere & Co. ( DE.N ) said it agreed to acquire tractor manufacturer Ningbo Benye Tractor & Automobile Manufacture Co. Ltd., located in southern China, to expand its product line.

title: Obama unveils plan to tackle housing crisis
text: Obama unveils plan to tackle housing crisis. MESA, Arizona - U.S. President Barack Obama pledged up to $275 billion on Wednesday to help stem a wave of home foreclosures, part of a broad effort using massive sums of government money to push the country out of recession.

title: Japan keeps verbal warnings, dollar up on debt deal
text: Japan keeps verbal warnings, dollar up on debt deal. TOKYO - Japan's finance minister kept up verbal intervention against a rising yen even as a weak dollar won a reprieve on Monday as U.S. lawmakers reached an agreement to raise the debt ceiling and avoid a sovereign default.

title: Netflix shares up 2.5 percent on news of iPhone app
text: Netflix shares up 2.5 percent on news of iPhone app. NEW YORK - Shares of Netflix Inc briefly extended their gains to 2.5 percent in afternoon trading on Monday after the company said it would bring a free app to Apple Inc's iPhone product this summer.

title: Caribbean's Millennium Bank is like Stanford: report
text: Caribbean's Millennium Bank is like Stanford: report. NEW YORK - Millennium Bank, a Caribbean-based institution, shares some attributes with Stanford International Bank, whose owner, Texas billionaire Allen Stanford, has been charged with fraud for offering high yields on certificates of deposit, Business Week wrote on its website on Tuesday.

text: Saving for stagflation. WASHINGTON - Here's a multiple-choice question for savers and investors: What's a more frightening prospect now, inflation or recession?

text: U.S. gasoline, diesel prices hit new records. WASHINGTON - The average price U.S. drivers paid for gasoline soared to a new high of $3.51 a gallon, rising 11.9 cents over the last week, the government said on Monday.

title: Dell to sell notebook PCs at U.S. Sam's Club stores
text: Dell to sell notebook PCs at U.S. Sam's Club stores. SAN FRANCISCO - Dell Inc. DELL.O said on Friday it would sell notebook computers at more than 580 of Wal-Mart Stores Inc.'s ( WMT.N ) Sam's Club outlets for $899 each starting next week, its latest move to sell computers in retail chains.

text: Volvo to cut 1,000 staff at Virginia plant. STOCKHOLM - Truck maker Volvo said on Monday it would cut about 1,000 staff at its Dublin, Virginia plant in the United States due to an expected decline in output.

title: BofA settles for $165 million with credit union regulator
text: BofA settles for $165 million with credit union regulator. WASHINGTON - Bank of America Corp ( BAC.N ) agreed to pay $165 million to settle charges by the U.S. credit union regulator involving sales of mortgage-backed securities to corporate credit unions that led them to fail, the regulator said on Tuesday.

title: Cyprus finance minister quits after bailout concludes, investigation begins
text: Cyprus finance minister quits after bailout concludes, investigation begins. NICOSIA - Cyprus's finance minister resigned on Tuesday after concluding a 10 billion euro bailout deal with international lenders in which the country slashed its dominant banking sector and hit depositors with losses.

title: Samsung chief to step down; sorry for tax scandal
text: Samsung chief to step down; sorry for tax scandal. SEOUL - South Korea's most powerful businessman on Tuesday announced he would step down as head of the giant Samsung Group following his indictment last week for tax evasion and breach of trust.

title: CVC group tables bid for Sainsbury: paper
text: CVC group tables bid for Sainsbury: paper. LONDON - A group of private equity firms led by CVC Capital has tabled an indicative offer of about 9.5 billion pounds ($18.75 billion) for UK supermarket chain J. Sainsbury ( SBRY.L ), the online edition of the Times newspaper reported on Thursday.

title: Lehman can pursue CDO claim: court
text: Lehman can pursue CDO claim: court. NEW YORK - Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc LEHMQ.PK can pursue claims on assets in a bankruptcy case expected to set a precedent for treatment of derivatives in complex investment products, a New York court said on Tuesday.

title: Ex-broker for Merrill, Deutsche Bank told to pay investor $11 million
text: Ex-broker for Merrill, Deutsche Bank told to pay investor $11 million. - U.S. securities arbitrators ordered a former employee of Merrill Lynch, Deutsche Bank and Oppenheimer & Co to pay nearly $11 million to an investor who alleged the broker misrepresented securities and made excessive trades.

title: Excerpt on policy from January FOMC minutes

text: Kimberly-Clark net down. CHICAGO - Kimberly-Clark Corp posted lower quarterly profit on Tuesday, hurt by higher interest expense.

text: ESPN president Bodenheimer "bullish" on ad growth. title: Trade gap widens in April as oil prices surge
text: Trade gap widens in April as oil prices surge. WASHINGTON - The U.S. trade deficit widened more than expected in April as the price of imported oil hit a record, pushing overall imports to an all-time high, a Commerce Department report showed on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive: ECB mulls ultra-long loans to help banks
text: Exclusive: ECB mulls ultra-long loans to help banks. BRUSSELS - The European Central Bank is looking at extending the term of loans it offers banks to 2 or even 3 years to try to prevent the euro zone crisis precipitating a credit crunch that chokes the bloc's economy, people familiar with the matter say.

title: Nintendo 06/07 sales, profit beat forecasts on DS
text: Nintendo 06/07 sales, profit beat forecasts on DS. TOKYO - Japanese video game maker Nintendo Co. 7974.OS raised its sales and profit forecasts for the fourth time on Thursday for the business year just ended, thanks to robust demand for its DS handheld games, sending its shares higher.

text: Bank of Montreal eyes LaSalle Bank assets: analyst. VANCOUVER, British Columbia - Bank of Montreal ( BMO.TO ) has indicated it would be interested in the Chicago-based assets of LaSalle Bank Corp. if they come on the market, a UBS analyst based in Toronto said on Monday.

title: Analysts view: No quick fix for D.Telekom's T-Mobile USA deal
text: Analysts view: No quick fix for D.Telekom's T-Mobile USA deal. FRANKFURT - Deutsche Telekom and AT&T withdrew their application for approval by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission of a planned $39 billion deal for T-Mobile USA to focus on obtaining the green light from the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ).

title: U.S. task force to convene on GM, Chrysler this week
text: U.S. task force to convene on GM, Chrysler this week. WASHINGTON - U.S. Treasury Secretary Tim Geithner and the White House will convene the Obama administration's task force on restructuring General Motors Corp and Chrysler LLC this week with the government, saying more would be required of the companies and their stakeholders.

title: Banks face exposure issues on Glencore-Xstrata merger
text: Banks face exposure issues on Glencore-Xstrata merger. LONDON - Glencore and Xstrata may have to put in place new multibillion dollar loans if their proposed $90 billion merger goes ahead, to help banks manage their huge exposures to the mammoth company, banking sources said on Tuesday.

text: Foundation blocks Arcelor Mittal's sale of Dofasco. BRUSSELS - A Dutch foundation holding the shares of Dofasco, Arcelor Mittal's ( ISPA.AS ) Canadian unit, said on Monday it had refused a request that would have allowed the sale of the unit to Germany's Thyssenkrupp ( TKAG.DE ).

text: Weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fall last week. WASHINGTON - The number of Americans filing new claims for jobless benefits unexpectedly fell last week, government data showed on Thursday, suggesting a modest improvement in the labor market.

text: Nokia Siemens Networks to slash staff by quarter. HELSINKI - Nokia Siemens Networks, the world's second-largest maker of mobile phone network equipment, is axing 17,000 jobs, nearly a quarter of its workforce, to help save about 1 billion euros ($1.35 billion) a year.

title: Skin cancer drug news boosts Bristol shares

text: Sohu Q2 net up 37 percent, sees Q3 revenue above Street view. - Chinese internet portal Sohu.com Inc ( SOHU.O ) posted a 37 percent increase in second-quarter net profit, helped by strong performance in its online games and brand advertising units and forecast third-quarter revenue above market estimates.

text: Cyprus cannot say when capital controls will be eased. NICOSIA - Cyprus hopes to ease capital controls as soon as possible but cannot say when that might happen, the island's Finance Minister Michael Sarris said on Tuesday.

text: BofA investor lawsuit wins class-action status. - Investors suing Bank of America Corp ( BAC.N ) won class-action status for their lawsuit accusing the bank of fraudulently misleading them about the 2008 takeover of Merrill Lynch & Co and the size of Merrill's losses and bonus payouts.

text: Consumer sentiment gains as gloom ebbs. NEW YORK - Consumer sentiment held up in late November as some of the gloom over the economic outlook ebbed, a survey released on Wednesday showed.

text: Oil seen above $100 by 2011 on shortages: Bernstein. NEW YORK - Oil prices may rise above $100 a barrel by early 2011, as global demand rises and producers fail to boost supply, Bernstein Research forecast on Monday.

text: AB InBev, Justice Department are near an agreement in beer deal. WASHINGTON - Anheuser-Busch InBev ( ABI.BR ) and the U.S. Justice Department have reached an agreement for a framework to settle their long-running beer brawl, and asked a court to extend a stay in the court fight until April 23, the two sides said in a court filing on Friday.

text: Europe factory sector almost stalls, Asia slows. SINGAPORE - China's factory activity slowed down in July and by one measure contracted as manufacturing across much of Asia weakened on signs that global demand is losing momentum.

text: McDonald's U.S. sales show consumer pullback. LOS ANGELES/CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp ( MCD.N ) on Tuesday posted its first monthly sales decline at established U.S. restaurants in five years, overshadowing strong overseas sales that produced higher-than-expected first-quarter profit.

text: U.S. hiring seen weaker in third quarter: Manpower. text: Congress, Obama playing with dynamite, CEOs say of "fiscal cliff".
